positiveControlBecauseAZeroIsAmbiguous.whyItWasNeeded: pdfinfo reports 'Form: none' on both delivered fixtures: they are fully flattened and carry no annotations at all, so every mark on a delivered page is content-stream ink. theNinePrintedNumbers.aSensitivityIFound: The bands are 15.61pt deep while the row pitch is 13.02-14.91pt, so consecutive rows' bands OVERLAP, and the module resolves a number to a row with Array.prototype.find rather than by unique containment. doTheGuardsActuallyFire.why: A guard that cannot fail is not a guard, and a lane's claim to have broken its own guard is exactly the claim that needs a second party. Every case below was run by this lane against the committed module, on a synthetic census carrying the real measured geometry of the question-1 charge table.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.premiseOneAllOrNothing: FIRES. Moving row 2's number to y=533.0, and separately moving row 3's number to y=493.0, each refuse with 'a printed row number was found beside 2 of them'.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.premiseTwoReadsAsAColumn: FIRES on both halves. Relabelling the printed numbers 3./2./1. down the page refuses. Moving one number 3pt off the column's left edge refuses; moving it 1.5pt, inside the 2pt tolerance, correctly passes.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.theSoundUnnumberedPage: PASSES CLEANLY. Removing all three number lines yields 'first row (the form prints no row numbers here)' and no refusal. This matters as much as the refusals: a guard that refuses sound pages is worse than no guard.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.lineGeometryGuard: FIRES. Deleting x from a printed line refuses with the left-edge message; deleting yExact refuses with the unrounded-baseline message.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.readingOrderBandSeparation: FIRES, and it is REACHABLE, which is not obvious. Because clustering is greedy against a seed that never moves, a band can admit a member exactly 4pt below its seed while the next item, 4.01pt below that same seed, is forced to open its own band 0.01pt away. Constructed and run: items at y = 531.08, 527.08, 527.07 refuse with 'two row bands are 0.01pt apart'. A gentler construction (531.08, 527.5, 526.9) refuses at 0.60pt. Clean rows 13pt apart pass.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.readingOrderBandSpread: UNREACHABLE, as FIX130 says. Over 200,000 randomly generated layouts of 2 to 6 items the maximum band spread observed was exactly 4.0000pt against a 4pt tolerance -- the bound is structural, not empirical, because every member joins by being within the tolerance of a seed that never moves. I confirm FIX130's decision to keep it and to label it unreachable: a pass there is not a measurement, and it is the assertion that would fail first if the seed ever became a running mean.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.theQuestionAsPut: Would a premise assertion catch a repin that nudged the printed number column out of band? Within the module: for any displacement up to roughly one row pitch, YES -- premise (1) fires, because the bands tile contiguously so a partial shift always leaves some rows matched and some not, and even a whole-column shift of 14pt lands the numbers in neighbouring bands and still fires. But a displacement large enough to clear every band at once -- I ran +50pt -- gives found = 0 for every group, and the module falls back SILENTLY to 'the form prints no row numbers here' on a page that still prints them. The module alone does NOT catch that case.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.whatDoesCatchIt: The host's pinned premise table. Running describeRowNumberGroups over the +50pt census returns all three charge-table groups as numbered=false, which the host's deepEqual reports as three 'appeared' entries and refuses the build with the groups named. So the layered claim holds: the module catches partial and mis-shaped columns, the host's pin catches the whole-column case, and neither alone is sufficient.
doTheGuardsActuallyFire.theTwoGuardDefectsFIX130Reports: Both are visible in the committed code and both are consistent with its account. The premise table now carries 27 entries -- 15 across 200-00130 and 200-00132 and 12 on 600-00228 -- so the fee-waiver's twelve groups are declared even though none of them reaches the participant's list. And the not-a-column check is written as an `if` followed by assert.fail rather than as assert.ok with a template message, with the reason recorded at the site; on the unnumbered path every entry of the printed array is null, so an assert.ok message template would have dereferenced null on 12 of this family's 15 groups and crashed every sound build. I confirm the shape of both fixes. I did not need to re-break the guard to see the second one, because the sound-page case above exercises exactly that path and passes.

thingsNoCounterCanSee: The shared module's own guards do not cover the whole-column case. A repin that moved the printed number column clear of every widget band leaves found = 0, and the module falls back silently to 'the form prints no row numbers here' on a page that still prints them. Only the HOST's pinned premise table refuses it. That matters for the migration FIX130 records as scheduled work: scripts/build-census-v1-vt_exp_decriminalized-set.mjs and scripts/build-census-v1-vt_seal_misdemeanor-set.mjs still carry hand-written copies, and neither carries any premise table -- grep finds no PRINTED_ROW_NUMBER_PREMISE and no assertPrintedRowNumberPremise in either. Rewiring those two hosts to import the module is therefore necessary but NOT sufficient: each also needs its own pinned shape table, or the families on them keep the silent-flip exposure this family has just been protected against. Recorded for the Captain; outside this lane's grant and not touched.

The nearest-printed-line caption heuristic is weaker across this family than the record says. 35 of the 46 requiredBeforeFiling rows carry a printedContext that does not contain the words of their own caption, and 18 of the 165 mapped rows read their caption from a line beneath the widget. Most are benign, but 200-00130 page 2 field 36 -- the interests-of-justice statement blank, the one blank the platform most emphatically refuses to write -- carries the text of question 5 as its printed context, and 200-00132 field 34g carries 'Email Address' for a mailing-address line. Neither is named in build-findings.json, which records only the 200-00132 fields 30-33 instance. Nothing participant-facing is wrong, because effectiveLabel is right on all 46; the exposure is that captionBasis advertises a heuristic whose output a reader would reasonably mistake for the caption. Recorded, not repaired.

The overlap between adjacent widget bands on the charge table means the module resolves a printed number to a row by first-match rather than by unique containment, with a smallest clearance of 2.82pt. It is safe today only because premise (2)'s strictly-increasing check would refuse the mis-assignment that overlap can produce -- which my own coarser measurement actually triggered. Worth knowing before anyone relaxes premise (2).

The canonical and boundary fixtures of 600-00228 share one sha256. A digest-collision check that assumes fixtures are distinct would flag it; it is in fact the correct signature of a component that is delivered unfilled in both profiles.
